body: Usually AliExpress sells international version of the Switch 2 console. However, according to the description, this particular console in a US model. articles.title: The Ultra-Slim Baseus Blade 20,000mAh Power Bank With 100W Output Drops to $39 for Black Friday
articles.summary: Looking for a high-capacity, high-output power bank with an ultra-slim footprint? Ahead of Black Friday, Amazon has dropped the price of the Baseus Blade 20,000mAh 100W power bank to just $39.49 shipped after you apply coupon code " Z6J1ANOV ". You do NOT have to be an Amazon Prime member.
body: The Baseus Blade measures only 0.7 inches thick. Most high-capacity power banks are well over 1" in thickness. The Blade achieves this slim depth by going with a wider body design. The form factor allows it to fit perfectly in a laptop bag or backpack sleeve. It still weighs in at about one pound which is comparable to other power banks, so no give or take there.

The wide body allows it to squeeze in four ports: two USB Type-C ports each with 100W of Power Delivery and two USB Type-A ports each with 30W output. Note that the maximum charging output is 100W. That means although all three ports add up to a total of 160W, only a maximum of 100W will be delivered across all three ports if they are used simultaneously.

The Baseus Blade has USB Type-C ports that provides up to 100W of power output but it will automatically throttle down to whatever maximum rate the plugged-in device accepts. The Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 can only accept a maximum of 18W-30W of power output. The Steam Deck can accept up to 45W. The Legion Go S accepts up to 55W. The Xbox ROG Ally X can actually accept charging rates of up to 100W.
points: Looking for a high-capacity, high-output power bank with an ultra-slim footprint?

articles.title: Steam’s Growing Review Backlog Has Cost Another Game Its Launch Date
articles.summary: Steam's growing backlog for approving game builds appears to be getting worse, as yet another studio's game is stuck in the purgatory of the platform's review program.
body: "Unfortunately, we're stuck waiting for Steam to review and approve our launch build. We have been waiting for a few weeks now and sadly don't know when they will finally get around to it," Australia Did It publisher Mystic Forge wrote in an update. "We're hoping to be able to launch as soon as possible and will update all of you the second we get an update. We really appreciate all of your continued support and apologize for the situation. We can't wait for you to check out the final game and hope to be able to get it into your hands soon!"

Australia Did It co-developer and game designer Rami Ismail said the game was originally submitted on October 20, and a minor controller issue caused it to fail. That bug was fixed the same day, but since then, Ismail and Aesthecian Labs have been stuck waiting for Steam approval.

articles.title: How About a GTA Set Outside the United States? 'Never Say Never,' Rockstar Boss Teases, but Don't Hold Your Breath
articles.summary: Rockstar isn't ruling out a GTA set outside the United States, but don't hold your breath: the studio says there are plenty more stories to tell in America. In an interview with The Guardian, Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson was asked whether or not the developer would ever make a GTA game…
body: The GTA series has largely rotated between three locations for the last 25 years: Liberty City (New York), Vice City (Miami), and San Andreas (California). We got a brief glimpse at the Midwest of GTA in GTA 5, when the game's story opened in a snowy state called North Yankton. But that's about as much as we've gotten outside of the coastal cities that GTA rotates through. It's unclear what else Rockstar wants to do with GTA, specifically the American setting.

GTA has flirted with going overseas before, as Rockstar came close to making one set in Japan in the early to mid-2000s. The first GTA also had an expansion set in London, and GTA 5 seemingly had scrapped DLC that would've at least partially taken place in Paris. Ex-GTA writer and creative director Dan Houser also stated last year that he doesn't think GTA would work as well outside of America.
points: Rockstar isn't ruling out a GTA set outside the United States, but don't hold your breath: the studio says there are plenty more stories to tell in America.

articles.title: WoW Forever's First Big Secret Has Been Discovered by Players
articles.summary: If there's one thing that's true about any version of World of Warcraft, it's that Blizzard loves hiding convoluted quest chains behind mundane objects, the first of which has been found in WoW Forever.
body: If you've started a Skyborne character in Forever, you've probably completed a quest that rewarded you with an 'Ancient Heirloom' ring with no stats, and wondered why it even exists. Well, it turns out that it kicks off a whole hidden quest chain if you know where to look.

This secret was discovered by the WoW Secret Finding and Collections Discord, and it involves getting that ring, finding a sword hilt that only shows up when you're using a specific torch, then finding a blade with a random location and then finding and cleansing a 'Befouled Water Globe.' The community has put together a guide on Wowhead of the known steps so far, but there's a catch – it doesn't seem like anyone has actually finished the little scavenger hunt yet.

As of this morning, folks in the WoW Secret Finding Discord are still actively trying to see what gets unlocked at the end of this convoluted chain, but for now, the community is calling it the "Dawn Waker Secret" and seems to believe it revolves around a couple of swords: Eluvi'ana and Eluvi'tor.

articles.title: Blizzard Can't Stop Tweaking WoW: Forever and It's Only Been 6 Days
articles.summary: While Blizzard has vowed to issue a major balance patch for World of Warcraft: Forever when the retro MMO's raids launch in December, the developer certainly doesn't seem afraid of doing some tinkering under the hood in the meantime. A roundup of hotfixes published on Nov.
body: Perhaps the most notable change is to gold rewards for questing during the higher levels, which have been increased. While many players have yet to reach this stage yet, Blizzard has come under fire for abandoning the conversion of XP into gold once you hit max level — a change applied not long before WoW 's first expansion, The Burning Crusade.

"We felt that it would be inappropriate for WoW: Forever players to be compelled to save up quests as they approach level 60 and then not turn them in until they transformed into a great profit," Blizzard explained. But this has left players at level 60 somewhat cash-strapped.

"In original WoW, only about 25% of quests in the game actually provide raw gold rewards, which led this to be a slightly more negative change than intended to gold income as you get closer to level 60," WoW: Forever 's community manager explained in another post. So Blizzard has added gold rewards to the majority of quests from level 48 onwards. "This change brings high-level quests in-line with the rest of questing in WoW: Forever, with the goal of giving players a good reason to complete those quests while leveling up to 60 and thereafter," Blizzard said.

articles.title: GTA 6 might be censored in Japan, if the game's smaller install size and lack of "strong sexual content" warning is anything to go by
articles.summary: GTA 6 is finally coming out worldwide next week, putting an end to a 13-year wait and at least one popular meme format, but the highly-anticipated game might look a bit different in Japan.
body: Now that pre-loading is live for the Rockstar Games mammoth, players across the globe can finally download the game and drool over its icon for the next week or so. But pre-orderers in Japan have noticed that GTA 6's file size comes to about 208GB on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores, versus up to 212GB in other regions.

As reported on by GameSpark and covered by Automaton, the game also received the strictest age rating from the Japanese certification board CERO - "Z" which is recommended for players aged 18 and over - but the listing notably doesn't contain one disclaimer seen in other international ratings.

PEGI and ESRB both warn of the game's "strong sexual content." Curiously, CERO's rating includes no such disclaimer. Together, some fans have taken the lack of "sexual content" disclaimer and smaller file size as signs that GTA 6 might not include some of the risque content we know it'll flaunt elsewhere in the world - based on NSFW leaks and a past rating that already clued us into the fact GTA 6 might be the first GTA to feature full-on sex scenes.

articles.title: Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum Officially Wraps Filming
articles.summary: We are one step closer to seeing a new Lord of the Rings film in theaters. Andy Serkis has confirmed that principal photography on The Hunt for Gollum has been completed, which he is directing in addition to reprising the titular role that made him famous.
body: Serkis broke the news during an interview on The Morning Mosh Pit, adding that he won't say too much about the film right now, because promoting it will be his focus all of next year. He did say that making The Hunt for Gollum has been "an incredible journey," which feels apt for a Lord of the Rings film. Jamie Dornan, who will take over the role of Aragorn from Viggo Mortensen for the film, similarly revealed to Variety that he had finished shooting his scenes about three weeks ago.

Dornan is an interesting part of The Hunt for Gollum, as one of the only actors stepping into a role played by someone else in Peter Jackson's Lord of the Rings trilogy. In addition to Serkis, both Elijah Wood and Ian McKellen are returning for the film to reprise their roles as Frodo Baggins and Gandalf, respectively. They'll all be joined by several newcomers playing original characters we haven't seen in live-action before, such as Kate Winslet as Marigol, Leo Woodall as Halvard, and Anya Taylor-Joy as Seren. The film is going to be something of an interquel to The Fellowship of the Ring, following Aragorn as Gandfalf sends him to capture Gollum to gain information on the One Ring.
points: We are one step closer to seeing a new Lord of the Rings film in theaters.

articles.title: Golden Joystick Awards 2026: All the Winners From Today’s Show
articles.summary: This year's gaming awards season kicks off in earnest today with the 44th annual Golden Joystick Awards. It's an especially interesting event given just how up in the air 2026's Game of the Year race has been.
body: There are two elephants in the room, however, with this year's Golden Joystick Awards. The first is Grand Theft Auto 6. Rockstar Games' much-anticipated blockbuster won't be released until Nov. 19, meaning it isn't in competition at this particular awards show. GTA 6 will undoubtedly upend the awards landscape, so later shows could look completely different than what we see today.

There is also the Big Walk issue. Developer House House revealed this week that it used AI, specifically large language models (LLMs), in the final phase of development. While the studio says that under 0.1% of the game's code had anything to do with generative AI tools, this will likely be a hardline for many that puts the critical darling out of contention. As The Golden Joystick Awards closed voting on Nov. 5, voters weren't aware of this controversy, but Big Walk winning awards may put a bad taste in some people's mouths that may be reflected in fewer accolades later this year.
Here's the complete list of winners from The Golden Joystick Awards 2026, which we will update as the show goes on.

articles.title: The European Commission's new Digital Fairness Act could change monetisation in games forever - and not just in Europe
articles.summary: The European Commission has published its proposed Digital Fairness Act, which has the potential to change how video games are monetised - worldwide - forever. A draft of the Act was leaked yesterday and what's been published today appears to be, to my eye, the same, though there's now also a…
body: And note that while the Digital Fairness Act isn't about video games exclusively - it's much broader than that - it does mention video games specifically, highlighting both their increased importance to society now, and that policy-shaping bodies like the European Commission are prepared to take them seriously.

The Digital Fairness Act is set to become European law, probably sometime between 2028 and 2029, once everyone's discussed it and made whatever amendments they're going to make to it. And at that point, breaching the regulations will come with potentially steep fines (up to six percent of a company's worldwide annual turnover, or up to €2m where an annual turnover isn't available).

The biggest things in the Digital Fairness Act relating to video games are regulations around loot boxes (sometimes referred to as "variable reward systems" or systems with "uncertainty-based rewards") and virtual currencies, particularly with regard to "minors" - anyone under 18 years old.
points: The European Commission has published its proposed Digital Fairness Act, which has the potential to change how video games are monetised - worldwide - forever.

articles.title: Hell Let Loose's original developers' Napoleonic-era extraction game, Hunger, gets December early access release, and an open beta this month
articles.summary: Good Fun Corp, the studio made up of the original developers behind Hell Let Loose, has finally announced a release date for its anticipated next project: Hunger. The extraction shooter-slasher game enters early access on Steam on 3rd December, and there's good news if you're eager to try it out…
body: Hunger's first and only open beta has also been announced, taking place 27th-29th November, the weekend prior to its early access launch. Unlike past tests, this one is available for anyone who requests access on Steam.

Though it may appear as yet another extraction shooter on the surface, Hunger offers more complex and intertwined systems than most. For one, combat has a focus on melee with only a few intentionally clunky firearms available. Though this is a PvPvE game, the vs environment side includes the sort of puzzle-solving, questing and dungeon-raiding typical of RPGs. The game's alternate history, plague-ravaged European setting gives it a grimey, steel-and-mud look few games have.

Beyond the in-match experience, Good Fun's ambitions extend to Hunger's MMO-style progression, its hub area with distinct characters and varied playable classes - all of which can be sampled in the upcoming beta.

Hunger just came off a very successful closed beta, which clearly didn't suffer by kicking off right alongside Modern Warfare 4's DMZ early access. Hunger is currently among Steam's most-wishlisted games, with over 700,000 wishlists, according to the developer.

articles.title: After being laid off by Microsoft, former Doom devs found new Smash TV-influenced FPS studio that isn't "subject to investor demands"
articles.summary: Back in July, Doom developers id Software laid off around a hundred people as part of wider Microsoft blood-letting. Now, a few of those devs have founded a new employee-owned studio, Hidden Horses.
body: Hidden Horses have 20 id Software alumni on the books, including former lead VFX artist Todd Boyce, principal engine programmer Dustin Land, senior AI and gameplay engineer Daniel Young, producer Andrew Willis, senior technical designer Jordan Turner, principal technical designer Tim Locke, and senior skybox artist Allison Dombek. They're looking to make "the kind of old school shooters that we think people want more of," in Land's words.

All members of Hidden Horses own a share of the company, with bosses "democratically" appointed, in the words of a FAQ. "Our structure is quite flat, and we elect leaders when needed," Willis told Vertical Slice in a separate interview. "Financially, this means we are not subject to investor demands and the preservation of the company and the jobs it sustains is paramount over needless growth and our 'capital' doesn't compete for returns with other potential investments."

All of which is obviously gesturing towards the horse elephant in the room: Microsoft, who've made enormous cuts to their Xbox biz in their eagerness to further supercharge their $4 trillion market value.

articles.title: "I wish hardware like the Xbox Series S wouldn't be released" - former Tekken director Katsuhiro Harada trashes Microsoft's console in front of senior Xbox staff
articles.summary: Katsuhiro Harada, formerly director on the Tekken series, is known for not pulling his punches. This truth was reinforced recently, as he said he wished the Xbox Series S "wouldn't be released" at a developer panel. All while a member of the Xbox team was in the room.
body: Per Inven Global, Harada was sitting on a panel at the Console Game Developers Conference 2026 in South Korea. The panel was moderated by former Sony president Shuhei Yoshida, and featured Shift Up CTO DongKi Lee ( Stellar Blade ), Too Kyo Games CEO Kazutaka Kodaka (Dangenrompa), CD Projekt Red associate game director Paweł Sasko ( Cyberpunk 2077 ), Ludeon Studios CEO Tynan Sylvester (Rimworld), and of course CEO of the newly formed VS Studio Katsuhiro Harada (Tekken).

The panel were asked about the advantages of console development, as well as specific challenges when creating games for certain platforms. Harada led the charge, speaking to the advantages consoles provide for fighting game developers, as the hardware is ideal for tournaments and esports events. Following this, he took an opportunity to speak about a console that drew his ire.

articles.title: I have converted GTA 5 from crime sim to train sim
articles.summary: Los Santos Customs. I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier.
body: As we've already discussed, I regard the personal automobile as a vector of poisonous ideology. Its beneficent alternative? The train: socialised, communal, predictable, subject to the gentle yet firm hand of rational state planning. If the world had more trains in it, we wouldn't be where we are now. We'd be somewhere else. On account of catching the train.

I have converted Grand Theft Auto 5's Franklin Clinton into one of the hero-drivers of these great iron beasts. I have installed Los Santos Metro Driver, which transforms Rockstar's opus from crime sim to train sim. Or tram sim, I guess. Same thing. The city's denizens need to move between airport terminals and only man can help them do it (you are that man).

Did you know driving trains, like, sucks? It's hard. You'd think it'd be easy, what with being essentially glued to your surface of operation, but I have spent most of my career as a trainee train-er overshooting platforms, accidentally applying the emergency brake, and sometimes running over passengers. Which, whatever.

body: Should consoles makers focus on price as hardware costs continue to skyrocket? An ex-Sony executive thinks so - but is a $300 PS5 even remotely achievable? In a similar vein, could cloud RAM work as a stopgap solution? Meanwhile, we discuss whether Xbox Helix could have a path tracing advantage over PS6 and how FSR 4 will affect comparisons between current-gen consoles. All this and more revealed in the latest DF Direct Q+A.

With the game currently sitting at an impressive 96 on Metacritic, the consensus is overwhelmingly positive.
